manual.how: NCVS Select: open https://api.ojp.gov/bjsdataset/v1/<id>.csv?$where=year='2024'&$limit=200000 in a browser (ids: gcuy-rt5g personal victimization, r4j4-fdwx personal population, gkck-euys household victimization, ya4e-n9zp household population) and save the CSV. Report tables: download https://bjs.ojp.gov/document/<code>.zip (e.g. cv24, p23st) from the report page. Upload the file with ingest.

cache.why: Datasets are replaced when a new year is added; data/ is reused within a run.

redistribution.why: BJS data and tables are U.S. government works in the public domain (17 U.S.C. 105); NCVS Select files are public-use, de-identified records.

citation: U.S. Department of Justice, Bureau of Justice Statistics, {dataset}, bjs.ojp.gov, retrieved {retrieved_long}.
clarify: Published estimate or own tabulation? BJS's report tables (statistical_table, e.g. cv24) carry the official numbers, rates and standard errors; tabulating NCVS Select records with the weights reproduces the numbers (2024 violent victimizations: 6,671,636 vs. 6,671,640 published), but standard errors need the survey design and are not computed here. Default: the report table when it has the breakdown asked for.

Victimizations, incidents or prevalence? NCVS counts victimizations by default (one per victim per crime); prevalence counts unique victims (weight wgt_ovam_per and the victim flag). Default: victimizations and the rate per 1,000 persons age 12 or older (households for property crime).
Which year? 2024 comes from the legacy half of a split sample (larger standard errors). Collection year: crimes are counted in the year of the interview, not the year they happened.
